fixes.explanation: Yes. Verse 57 says, “But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.” Cutting out the mildewed section was the step before (Leviticus 13:56). Once the mildew shows up again, the text says burn it.

White hair plus a sore that appears to be deeper than the skin settles it. Verse 3 says, “…it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.” Those two signs together are what the priest is looking for in that verse. So the verdict is unclean.

Shaving does come up in this chapter, but later, for a scaly outbreak (Leviticus 13:33). Here the priest sees white hair and a sore that appears to be deeper than the skin. Verse 3 says that in this case, “…it is a skin disease.” So he pronounces the person unclean instead of waiting. Seven days apart is for when the spot doesn't appear deeper and the hair hasn't turned white (Leviticus 13:4).

No river in this passage, friend. When washing comes up, it's clothes, and it comes after the person is pronounced clean (Leviticus 13:6, 34). Here the priest pronounces the person unclean (Leviticus 13:3). No river trip in that verse, so my apron stays dry.

I see why it feels that way, since nothing changed and nothing spread. But verse 5 says the priest “…must isolate him for another seven days.” Staying the same isn't being pronounced clean yet. The text gives another week, and it doesn't say where the person spends it.

Right, not clean yet. Verse 5 says that if the infection is unchanged and hasn't spread, “…the priest must isolate him for another seven days.” A second week, then the priest examines again (Leviticus 13:6). The ruling comes after that.

Clean is the word. Verse 6 says that if the sore has faded and hasn't spread, “…the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash.” The person must also wash his clothes and be clean. That's where the two weeks of waiting end.

Unclean is the ruling when the rash has spread (Leviticus 13:8). Here the sore has faded and has not spread. Verse 6 says in that case, “…the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash.” So this one goes the other way.

Diseased isn't the word the priest uses here. When the sore has faded and has not spread, verse 6 says he “…shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash.” Skin disease is what he says when the rash has spread (Leviticus 13:8). So clean is the ruling in this case.

Scar is a word the chapter uses elsewhere, for a spot after a boil or a burn that is unchanged and hasn't spread (Leviticus 13:23, 28). This rash has spread, though. Verse 8 says, “…it is a skin disease.” So the priest doesn't call it a scar.

Those two don't make the priest say unclean. Seven days apart is for a spot with no white hair in it, not beneath the skin, and faded (Leviticus 13:21). Black hair comes up later, when a scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it (Leviticus 13:37). So this pair isn't the unclean signs.

Yes. Verse 33 says, “…the person must shave himself except for the scaly area.” Then the priest isolates him for another seven days. On the seventh day, the priest examines the scaly outbreak again (Leviticus 13:34).

Covering with a cloth isn't in this verse. The text says the person must shave except for the scaly area (Leviticus 13:33). After that, the priest isolates him for another seven days. That's the step, and no cloth is mentioned.

Harmless is the word. Verse 39 says, “…if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.” Dull white is the sign in this case. This is the paint-swatch part of the chapter.

Yes. Verse 46 says, “As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp.” That is the place the text gives for a person who has the infection. I think this one hurts to read.
The text doesn't put the person there. Verse 46 says, “He must live alone in a place outside the camp.” The Tent of Meeting isn't mentioned in that verse. The words are alone, and outside the camp.

No, the text says something else. Verse 46 says the person “…must live alone in a place outside the camp.” The priests' families aren't mentioned in that verse. Alone and outside the camp is what it says.

The text says the priest isolates the item. Verse 50 says he is to “…isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.” Handing it back isn't a step in the text. Seven days of isolation come first, then he examines it again (Leviticus 13:51).

The priest isolates the item during the seven days (Leviticus 13:50), but that isn't how it ends. Once the mildew has spread, verse 52 says, “…the article must be burned up.” Keeping it isn't the instruction.
